info.title: MonitorFlow public API
info.description:
The public API of MonitorFlow, for scripts and integrations: a PSA reading alerts, a chat bot acknowledging them, an Ansible play silencing a server during a deployment. It is the same API the web interface uses, under `/api/v1`, with the same rules about who may see and change what.

## API keys

An administrator makes a key under **Admin › API keys**: a global administrator for anything, a customer's administrator for that customer, a site's administrator for that site. The key is shown once, when it is made: `mfk_` followed by 43 characters. MonitorFlow keeps only a hash of it, so a lost key cannot be shown again; make another one.

What a key may do is chosen when it is made and never changes. To change it, make another key and turn the first one off.

- **Access**: "Read only" (viewer, the default), "Read and change" (operator), "Approve commands" (approver) or "Administer" (administrator).
- **Reach**: everything, one customer or one site. Outside its reach, servers, sites and incidents do not exist for the key: they answer 404, and lists leave them out.
- **Areas**, all by default: `servers` (servers and relays, their metrics and logs), `alerts` (incidents, silences, on-call, follow-up, sensors, thresholds and check settings, offline alerts, notification channels), `updates` (commands, campaigns, packages, package sources, mirrors, rollback, update settings), `remediation` (AI remediation and AI commands), `dashboards`, and `administration` (everything else). A route outside the key's areas answers 403 `api_key_scope`. Any key may list servers, relays, sites and customers within its reach, to turn names into IDs. Each operation below says which area it belongs to.
- **Expiry**: 30 days, 90 days, 1 year (the default) or never.

A key acts as the person who made it, narrowed to its reach and access, checked again on every request. It never does more than its maker could at that moment: a maker who loses a role loses it for the key too, a maker who is disabled finds the key refused, and a maker who is deleted takes the key with them. The keys list shows when each key was last used, to the minute. Anyone who could have made a key can turn it off; it stops at its next request.

What a key changes is written to the audit log as its maker's action, with the key's ID, so the log tells a person from their script. The secret never appears in the audit log or the server's logs.

## Authentication

Send the key in the `Authorization` header of every request:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer mfk_…" https://monitorflow.example.com/api/v1/servers
```

Keys work only under `/api/v1`; the web interface's own paths refuse them. A request with a key needs no CSRF header. A missing, malformed, unknown or expired key, or one whose maker is disabled, answers 401 `unauthenticated`.

Signing in and out, first-run setup, password and acknowledge links, display links and screens, API keys themselves, a person's own on-call contact, and inviting users or issuing their password links are not part of the public API: they answer 404 under `/api/v1`. They are for people in a browser, or they hand out a credential that would outlive the key.

## Versions and changes

`/api/v1` is a contract. Within v1, MonitorFlow only adds: new fields in answers, new optional parameters, new routes, new values of `code`. Fields are never renamed or removed and their types never change. Your client must ignore fields it does not know. When a change would break v1, MonitorFlow keeps the old shape in v1 and makes a v2 only when that becomes unreasonable.

This document is served by every central server at `/api/v1/openapi.json`, without a key.

## Conventions

- Bodies are JSON objects with `snake_case` field names. Send `Content-Type: application/json`. Bodies are at most 64 KiB; a larger one answers 413. Most routes refuse a body with a field they do not know, with 400 `invalid`.
- IDs are UUIDs. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC, like `2026-11-14T09:30:00Z`. Durations are in seconds (`_s`) or milliseconds (`_ms`), as the field name says.
- An ID that is not a UUID answers 404, like an ID that does not exist.

## Pagination

Lists that can grow without bound take `limit` and `cursor` and answer `next_cursor`: servers, relays, incidents, commands, campaigns, tokens, remediation incidents and events. Pass `next_cursor` as `cursor` to get the next page, with the same filters; it is `null` on the last page. Cursors are opaque: do not build or change them. A server or incident added between two pages neither repeats nor shifts the others. There are no page numbers or totals.

Lists that stay small (sites, customers, silences, approvals, dashboards) answer in full.

## Filters

Filters are query parameters, exact values ANDed together, like `GET /api/v1/incidents?state=open&severity=critical&site_id=…`. A bad value is 400 `invalid`, and so is an unknown parameter on the lists that say so.

## Errors

Every error answers with a status and a JSON body:

```json
{"error": "limit must be between 1 and 500", "code": "invalid"}
```

`error` is a sentence in plain words, safe to show to a person; it may change between versions. `code` is stable: branch on it. Codes are only ever added.

| Code | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | 400 | The body could not be read as JSON (most routes answer `invalid` instead, with the parser's message) |
| `invalid` | 400 | A parameter or field is wrong; `error` says which and why |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | No key, or one that is unknown, expired or turned off, or whose maker is disabled |
| `invalid_credentials` | 401 | Wrong username or password (signing in, not in v1) |
| `forbidden` | 403 | The key's access, or its maker's roles, do not allow this on something it can see |
| `api_key_scope` | 403 | The route is outside the key's areas |
| `cross_site` | 403 | A browser request without the CSRF header (sessions only) |
| `not_found` | 404 | It does not exist, or is outside the key's reach |
| `conflict` | 409 | The current state does not allow it, like a silence already over; `error` says why |
| `idempotency_in_progress` | 409 | The first request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still running |
| `gone` | 410 | A one-time link that was used or expired (not in v1) |
| `idempotency_key_reused` | 422 | This `Idempotency-Key` was used for another request |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Over the key's rate limit |
| `internal` | 500 | Something failed on the central server; the details are in its log |
| `metrics_unavailable` | 502 | The metrics database is unreachable, failing or not configured |
| `logs_unavailable` | 502 | The logs database is unreachable, failing or not configured |
| `metrics_timeout` | 504 | The metrics database did not answer in time |
| `logs_timeout` | 504 | The logs database did not answer in time |

## Idempotency keys

A `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE` made with a key may carry `Idempotency-Key`: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The first request with a value runs and its answer is kept for 24 hours. The same request again (same method, path, query and body) gets that answer back with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, instead of running a second time. A script that lost its connection can then retry without opening two silences or queuing two updates.

- The same value with another request answers 422 `idempotency_key_reused`.
- While the first request is still running, a retry answers 409 `idempotency_in_progress`; try again a moment later.
- Answers of 500 and above are not kept, so a retry runs again. Answers over 1 MiB are not kept either.
- Answers that hand out a secret once (tokens, install keys, signing secrets) are not stored: a replay says it was done, without the secret.
- Values belong to a key: two keys never see each other's answers.

Without the header, writes behave as usual. Most are safe to repeat anyway, like acknowledging an incident or setting a value; the operations that are not say so.

## Rate limits

Each key may make 600 requests a minute, counted in fixed one-minute windows on each central server. Every answer to a key carries:

- `RateLimit-Limit`: requests allowed in a window, 600.
- `RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window.
- `RateLimit-Reset`: seconds until the window ends.

Over the limit, requests answer 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`, in seconds. Requests made in a browser session are not limited.

post.description:
Adds a customer, without sites; add them with `POST /api/v1/customers/{id}/sites`.

**Who**: a global administrator; the key must reach everything with "Administer" access. **Area**: `administration`.

Names are 1 to 64 characters, without control characters or spaces at either end, and unique. Audited as `customer.create`. Sending the same name twice is refused with 409, so a retry never makes two customers.

Changes a customer's name. Only the name changes: its sites, servers, roles and API keys refer to its ID and keep working.

**Who**: a global administrator; the key must reach everything with "Administer" access. **Area**: `administration`.

Adds a site to a customer. Servers join it when they are installed with one of its install commands. Sites never move between customers.

**Who**: an administrator of the customer as a whole: a global administrator, or one of that customer. A site administrator may not, and neither may a key that reaches one site. **Area**: `administration`.

Names are 1 to 64 characters, without control characters or spaces at either end, and unique across all customers: the name is the `site` label of every metric. Audited as `site.create`. Sending the same name twice is refused with 409.

get.description:
The value of one metric of one server at `time` (now by default): one series per instance, or one with `agg`. `query` in the answer is the query MonitorFlow ran, for reference.

`metric` is `monitorflow_` followed by a sensor's metric name, such as `monitorflow_cpu_usage_ratio`; `GET /api/v1/servers/{id}/metrics` lists those a server reported. `instance` is what the sensor watches, like a disk or a service. `lookback` (1 to 172800 seconds) takes the last value within that window, for checks that run less often than every few minutes.

**Who**: any role on the server's site. **Area**: `servers`.

Answers hold at most 500 series. Unknown parameters are 400.

parameters.name: server_id
parameters.description: The server whose metric to read.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Full name, `monitorflow_<sensor metric>`.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description:
What the sensor watches, like `/var` or `total`; every instance when
absent.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: Defaults to now.

parameters.name: agg
parameters.description: Combines the series into one: `avg`, `min`, `max`, `sum` or `count`.

parameters.name: lookback
parameters.description:
1 to 172800 seconds: the last value within this window rather than within
VictoriaMetrics' default, for checks that run less often (ADR-0097).

get.description:
One metric of one server from `start` to `end` (the last hour by default), a point every `step` seconds (by default the range over 720, at least 1). Points are `[unix seconds, value]`; a value that is not a finite number is `null`.

Without `rollup`, a point is the last sample before it, so a short spike between two points of a long range does not show. With `rollup` (`avg`, `max`, `min`, `last`), each point summarizes its series over the step before it, before `agg` combines the series: `rollup=max` keeps the spikes.

**Who**: any role on the server's site. **Area**: `servers`.

Ranges are at most 31 days and under 11,000 points per series; answers hold at most 500 series. Unknown parameters are 400.

parameters.name: server_id
parameters.description: The server whose metric to read.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Full name, `monitorflow_<sensor metric>`.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description:
What the sensor watches, like `/var` or `total`; every instance when
absent.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Defaults to `end` minus one hour.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Defaults to now.

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: Seconds; defaults to the range over 720, at least one second.

parameters.name: agg
parameters.description: Combines the series into one: `avg`, `min`, `max`, `sum` or `count`.

parameters.name: rollup
parameters.description: Applied per series over a window of one step, before `agg`.

400.description: A bad metric name or instance, `start` not before `end`, a range over 31 days, too many points, a bad `step`, an unknown parameter, more than 500 series, or a query the metrics database refused: `invalid`

get.description:
One page of the servers within the key's reach, sorted by site name, then hostname, then name. Removed servers are left out; read one by its ID to see it.

**Who**: any key, whatever its areas. A key whose maker has no role at all is 403.

**Pages**: `limit` servers per page, 1 to 1000, 500 by default. Pass `next_cursor` as `cursor` for the next page; it is `null` on the last one. Other query parameters are ignored.

`status` is `online` while the agent has a connection open, directly or through a relay. A connected agent that has no server yet (waiting for approval) is not listed.

incident_ids.description: 1 to [`MAX_LIMIT`] incidents, like a group of a notification.

Acknowledged.description:
Body of the answer: the incidents this request acknowledged. The
others were resolved, or someone acknowledged them first.

Aggregation.description: A simple aggregation across the selected series.

AiCommandsChange.description: The last `ai_commands` command of a server, in `GET /api/servers/{id}`.

requested_by.description: The username, `null` when the account is gone.

command.description: Runs this instead of the proposal, recorded as an `edit`.

CommandDetail.description:
`GET /api/commands/{id}`: the command and its output, each at most
the last 64 KiB.

health_timeout_s.description:
`self_update`: seconds the new agent has to connect before the
old one comes back; 30 to 3600, 300 by default.

packages.description: Packages to upgrade; empty or absent for all.

ttl_s.description:
Seconds the agent may still start it; [`MIN_TTL_S`] to
[`MAX_TTL_S`], default [`DEFAULT_TTL_S`].

parameters.description: The payload as JSON, for kinds the API knows.

site_count.description: Sites of the customer the user reads, not all of them.

command.description: What will run, or what was rejected.

Error.description: Every error: a sentence to show and a stable code to branch on.

code.description: Stable; codes are only ever added.

error.description: Plain words, safe to show; may change between versions.

details.description:
For instance `{"reason": "threshold_removed"}`, `{"notified":
true}` when a silence ended, `{"username", "via"}` when
acknowledged, or `{"step", "steps", "minutes", "told"}` for a
follow-up step.

kind.description:
`opened`, `escalated`, `deescalated`, `resolved`, what a silence
did: `silenced` and `silence_ended` (ADR-0079), `acknowledged`, and
`followed_up` when a follow-up step told someone (ADR-0082).

occurred_at.description: Sample time of the change, or the server clock without a sample.

severity.description: Severity after the change; `null` once resolved.

FollowUpView.description: Where an incident is in its follow-up.

next.description: Who it would tell then, people first; empty when nobody can be.

next_at.description: When the next step is told if nobody acknowledges.

started_at.description: When the first message went out.

state.description:
`waiting` for the next step at `next_at`, `silenced` until a silence
ends then waiting, or `stopped`.

step.description: Steps told so far, and how many there are now.

stop_reason.description:
When stopped: `acknowledged`, `resolved`, `not_critical`, or
`finished` once every step was told.

GroupView.description: A notification that told this incident with others (ADR-0080).

incidents.description:
How many incidents it told that the user may read, this one
included. Members on sites outside the user's scope are not counted.

GuestKind.description: What a Proxmox guest is, which picks its API path.

oneOf.description:
Who is told next if nobody acknowledges (ADR-0082); `null` when no
follow-up started: a warning, or not sent yet.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

IncidentView.description:
One incident. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

acknowledged_by.description:
Who said they are on it, and when (ADR-0082); `null` until someone
does. The name stays when the account is removed.

can_acknowledge.description:
Whether the reader may acknowledge it: open, not acknowledged, and
the reader an operator or above of its site.

hostname.description: The server's hostname, or the relay's name.

instance.description: `""` for a series without an instance.

metric.description: `offline` when the server or relay stopped reporting (ADR-0072).

opened_at.description: Sample times, not the server clock.

peak_value.description: The worst value seen while open.

relay_id.description: Set for a relay's offline incident only (ADR-0072).

severity.description: `warning` or `critical`; the last one while resolved.

silenced.description: Whether a silence ever held back a notification of it.

silenced_until.description:
While open and covered by a silence, when the last one ends
(ADR-0079).

threshold.description: The threshold as it was when the incident opened.

name.description:
1 to 64 characters, without control characters or spaces at either
end.

PendingView.description:
One command waiting for approval. Field names and types are part of
the API contract: add fields, never rename or remove them.

can_approve.description:
Whether the user may approve this command as proposed, and reject
it. UX hints: the decision routes check again.

command.description: The proposed command, exactly as it would run.

commands_run.description: Commands the incident ran so far, and its limit.

deadline.description:
`opened_at + max_duration_s`: the incident escalates then, and a
decision after it is 409.

diagnosis.description: The AI's text: untrusted, shown as data.

id.description: The pending command; decisions go to `/approvals/{id}/...`.

shell.description:
What runs the command: `posix` (`/bin/sh`) or `powershell`
(Windows PowerShell), from the server's system (ADR-0084).

shell_acceptance.description:
What the server's agent last said it does with these commands:
`accepted`, `off`, `unsupported`, or `null` when unknown (ADR-0076).
Approving is 409 once it refuses them.

snapshots.description:
Whether a change on this server is snapshotted first, on Proxmox
(ADR-0044) or locally (ADR-0094); when not, rollback is limited.

tier.description: `low_impact` or `high_impact`, from the rules, never from the AI.

query.description: The PromQL the API ran, filters included.

reason.description: Sent back to the AI with the rejection, and recorded.

Rollup.description:
How each point of a range summarizes the samples since the previous
point. Without it, a point is the last sample before it, so a spike
between two points of a long range is not drawn.

SeriesView.description:
One series: its labels and its `[unix seconds, value]` points. A value
that is not finite is `null`.

labels.description:
`__name__`, `instance`, `peer` (the server's name) and `site`, or
none once aggregated.

oneOf.description:
The last time AI commands were turned on or off from the web
interface, `null` if never (ADR-0098).

The certificate issued last to this agent, revoked or not; `null`
when the CA never issued one (a server row created by hand).

ServerDetail.description:
Body of `GET /api/servers/{id}`: the listing row plus the agent's
current certificate.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

servers.description: By site name, hostname and name.

ServerView.description:
One server. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

agent_version.description: Version reported by the live stream, else the one last stored.

cert_not_after.description:
Latest expiry among the agent's unrevoked certificates; `null` when
it has none. Past dates mean every certificate has expired.

command_kinds.description:
What its agent last said it does with each command kind: `accepted`,
`off` or `unsupported` (ADR-0076). `null`, or a kind missing here, is
unknown: its agent or a relay on the way does not report yet.

connected_at.description: Start of the current stream, when online.

hostname.description: The machine's host name, as its agent reports it.

last_heartbeat.description:
Last message received: from the live stream when online, else the
last time recorded in the database.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether it opens an incident when offline (ADR-0072); muted when
this or `site_offline_alerts` is `false`.

open_incidents.description: Threshold and offline incidents currently open on this server.

os_version.description: Like `12` or `9.4`; `null` until the agent reports it.

package_updates.description: Whether the host can take package updates and sources (ADR-0063).

peer_id.description:
The agent's name, given when it was installed; the `peer` label of
its metrics.

relay_id.description: The relay its last connection came through; `null` when direct.

revoked_at.description: When it was removed; `null` while it is in the fleet.

silenced_until.description: While a silence covers it, when the last one ends (ADR-0079).

via_relay.description: Peer ID of the relay carrying the live stream, if any.

Shell.description: The shell that runs a server's commands, which decides the rules.

target_id.description: The server, relay, site or customer; absent for `all`.

can_end.description: Whether this user may end it.

agent_auto_update.description:
The site's automatic update override: `null` follows the
server-wide setting (ADR-0055).

agent_auto_update_effective.description: Whether automatic updates apply to the site, override or not.

name.description: Unique across customers; the `site` label of every metric.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether servers and relays of the site open incidents when offline
(ADR-0072).

relay_count.description: Relays of the site, removed ones left out.

server_count.description: Servers of the site, removed ones left out.

SnapshotSupport.description:
Whether the server can be snapshotted; without it the interface shows
that rollback is limited.

detail.description:
With `cannot_snapshot`: what Proxmox cannot snapshot, like "rootfs
is on storage local (dir), which cannot take snapshots".

oneOf.description: The mapped guest's kind, so the reason can say VM or container.

left_out.description: What a snapshot does not hold, though Proxmox takes one.

method.description:
Which snapshot a change gets when available: `proxmox`, or a local
`lvm` or `zfs` snapshot (ADR-0094).

Tier.description: Risk tiers of architecture §8, from least to most dangerous.

api_key.description: An API key made under Admin › API keys: `Authorization: Bearer mfk_…`. It acts as its maker, narrowed to its reach, access and areas.

tags.name: servers
tags.description: The servers MonitorFlow watches: one machine each, with its agent. Lists and details carry the live connection status, open incidents, silences and certificate expiry. Area `servers`; any key may list servers within its reach.

tags.name: sites
tags.description: Sites group servers and relays, usually one per place or network; customers own sites. A single company has one customer. Sites and customers are listed by any key within its reach; creating them is in the `administration` area.

tags.name: alerts
tags.description: Incidents are opened and resolved by MonitorFlow when a threshold is crossed or a server stops reporting; the API reads and acknowledges them. Silences stop notifications about a server, relay, site, customer or everything for a while. Area `alerts`.

tags.name: updates
tags.description: Commands sent to a server's agent: package updates and agent updates, queued, sent as soon as the agent is connected, with their output. Area `updates`.

tags.name: remediation
tags.description: Commands the AI proposed to fix an incident that the rules held for a person: approve, edit or reject them. The AI's text is untrusted and shown as data. Area `remediation`.

tags.name: metrics
tags.description: Values a server's sensors reported, now or over a range. You name a server, a metric and optionally an instance; MonitorFlow builds the query itself and never accepts raw PromQL. Area `servers`.
